chunks: Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the woman whose husband dies, should she observe her waiting period in a house, remaining in it for a month, or less than a month, or more, then move from it to another, so she remains in the house she moved to for a period similar to what she remained in the house she moved from? Such is her practice until her waiting period is completed. He said: That is permissible for her, and there is no problem.

key_terms.الْمُتَوَفَّى عَنْهَا زَوْجُهَا: The woman whose husband has died (widow)

ai.seo_question: Can a widow move to a different house while observing her waiting period (iddah)?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the flexibility of the widow's waiting period (iddah) by permitting her to change residences, provided the duration of absence from one home is matched by the stay in the next to maintain continuity. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on practical ease (taysir) for the widow, allowing her to adapt her living situation without invalidating the prescribed four months and ten days. It underscores that the iddah is a temporal obligation tied to the passage of time rather than strict confinement to a single physical location.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from a man, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the woman widowed from her husband, should she wait in a house, remaining in it for a month, or less than a month, or more, then transfer from it to another, so she remains in the house which she moved to similar to what she remained in the house she moved from. Such is what she does until she fulfils her waiting period. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘That is allowed for her, and there is no problem’.
en.sarwar: 7. Humayd has narrated from ibn Sama‘ah from ‘Abd Allah ibn Jabalah from ibn Bukayr from ‘Ubayd ibn Zurarah who has said the following: “I once asked abu Ibrahim, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a woman whose husband dies;
if she can go out of the house of her husband. He (the Imam) said, ‘She can go out of the house of her husband, travel for al-Hajj or move from one house to another house.’”
